name: LDAP / Directory Access
description: LDAP and directory access — also called LDAP bind, directory query, the LDAP search, or directory authentication — the flow where an application or service connects to an LDAP directory and authenticates (bind) or reads / writes directory entries (search, compare, modify): OpenLDAP (slapd) and FreeIPA over ldap:// (389) or ldaps:// (636) / StartTLS, used both as an authentication backend (bind to verify user credentials) and as an identity / group lookup. Distinct from the web-SSO Authentication Exchange (OIDC / SAML) and from the generic Database Query, though it shares their injection and transport concerns. The place to look for LDAP, directory bind / search, the LDAP server query, or directory-based authentication and group lookup. Its threat surface: anonymous or unauthenticated bind, cleartext LDAP on 389 without TLS / StartTLS exposing bind credentials and entries, LDAP injection via unescaped search filters, over-permissive directory ACLs disclosing the full directory tree, and a privileged bind-DN credential exposed in application config.
